title: Read an invoice PDF and work out the amount due with late interest

source.changes: Instruction is the source's goal, word for word. The source's invoice is an 82,787-byte LaTeX-made PDF (tasks/definitions/native/assets/invoice.pdf); ours is a one-page text PDF in Courier with the same text and figures, typed out again so it can travel inline in an exec argument (setup adds the cross-reference table). The source's printed subtotal (85,100.00) is not the sum of its line items (84,100.00); we kept the figures as printed. The source's key, 104417.7, is the printed total due (102,120.00) plus 1.5% a month for 45 days (2.25%); the same rule applied to the line items' sum with 20% VAT gives 103,190.70, and the check takes either. The source parsed the answer as a number after dropping commas; ours takes the number with or without thousands commas and a leading $, and trailing zeros. The source reset Chrome first; this port doesn't, and the source's own check reads only the answer. The answer is the agent's final answer, so there is no oracle.

setup.why: Write the invoice to /sdcard/Download/invoice.pdf (moving a file already there aside) and ask the media scanner to list it.

instruction: Read the invoice PDF file in the download directory. The customer has notified that payment will be made 45 days after the due date. Please recalculate the total amount payable and respond with only a single number representing the total amount, with no other text.

checks.why: The final answer is only the amount: 104,417.70 (the printed total due, 102,120.00, plus 1.5% a month for 45 days) or 103,190.70 (the same from the line items' sum, which is 1,000 under the printed subtotal), with or without thousands commas, a leading $ and trailing zeros. An agent that answers nothing fails.

teardown.why: Delete the run's invoice, put back a file setup moved aside, and go home.
